title: Senior's toolkit: dependencies, artifacts and secrets
summary: dotnet list package and npm audit with the flags that matter, an SBOM in one command, cosign to sign and verify, gitleaks in every stage, and git log -S to find when a secret arrived.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: dependencies, artifacts and secrets
steps.body: Supply-chain work is mostly automation: the same checks on every build, so a bad package or a leaked key is caught by a machine before a person has to.

toolkit.what: Every package with a known advisory, direct and transitive, per project and framework. --format json feeds a CI gate.
flags: fail restore on high and critical advisories
toolkit.example: dotnet list Shop.sln package --vulnerable --include-transitive --format json > vulnerable.json

toolkit.what: The same for JavaScript dependencies, from the lock file. `npm ci` (not `npm install`) in CI installs exactly what the lock file says.
flags: exit non-zero only for high and critical

toolkit.what: Produce a CycloneDX SBOM for a solution: every component and version, ready for Dependency-Track or a vulnerability database. (Microsoft's sbom-tool produces SPDX.)
Sigstore's tool to sign container images and other artifacts (keyless, with the CI system's identity) and to verify them before deploy, so only images your pipeline built can run.
flags: sign by digest, never by tag
attach the SBOM as a signed attestation

toolkit.what: Find secrets in a repository's whole history, in staged changes before a commit, or in a folder. Newer versions use `gitleaks git` and `gitleaks dir`; 8.16 (Debian, the lab) uses `detect` and `protect`.
flags: scan every commit, show each finding
pre-commit: only what is about to be committed
a plain folder (8.16); `gitleaks dir` in newer versions

toolkit.what: Every commit, on every branch, that added or removed a string: when did the secret arrive, and who else has it.
flags: commits that change how often text appears
commits whose diff matches a regex

steps.prompt: Match each command to the question it answers.
pairs: Which of our packages have advisories?
What exactly is in this release?
Did our pipeline build this image?
When did this string enter the history?

steps.prompt: Pre-commit: scan only the staged changes. CI: scan the whole history and write a report.
The pipeline signs images by tag (`cosign sign ghcr.io/shop/web:1.4`). Why do reviewers ask for the digest instead?
options: A tag can be moved to another image; a digest names exactly one image, so the signature covers exactly what was built
